articles.full_text:
PUDUCHERRY: The Yanam region of the Union territory of Puducherry, about 800km from the headquarters, has been placed on red alert as very severe cyclonic storm Arnab is likely to cross the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam in the neighbouring Andhra Pradesh near the region on Wednesday.
The Puducherry administration has taken all precautionary measures in Yanam to face the onslaught of the very severe cyclonic storm. Two companies of the
National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) alongside a 33-member State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) team from Puducherry have reached Yanam to handle emergencies, spearhead rescue and relief operations.
The administration has urged residents to stock up on essentials, keep essential utility services (power and water) on standby, and strictly stay indoors as the cyclone approaches landfall. It has released dedicated help line numbers (8885613111, 9391149707 and 9032093583) for relief, rescue, and medical assistance. The residents have been advised to avoid unnecessary travel, remain indoors during peak surge hours, and reach out to officials via the helpline numbers in case of emergency.
A total of 19 relief camps have been established in local schools. Due to ongoing rains, 552 residents living in 142 vulnerable thatched huts in low-lying areas, along with 52 differently abled individuals, have already been safely evacuated and relocated to these camps.
Five pregnant women nearing full term have been identified and admitted to the local primary health centre. They are under continuous medical observation by dedicated healthcare teams.
All schools and colleges across the Yanam region have been declared closed for two days (Tuesday and Wednesday). All liquor shops in Yanam will remain closed from 4pm on Tuesday till Oct 29 to maintain public order and safety during the disaster. Public works minister Malladi Krishna Rao has urged residents to exercise extreme caution, warning that the impact of Arnab will increase from Tuesday night. He urged people residing in thatched huts, kutcha structures, and damaged houses to immediately move to designated govt relief camps as a precautionary measure.
